open_points.subject: A20 running-dependency invariant
open_points.text:
None: kept by the release process and its installation outside Registry
(rule 5) — the running dependencies are the release's (name, version,
digest), which no note or check of Registry's code can show.
open_points.question: Is “a running instance uses exactly the dependencies named by its release” a formal invariant of the installed release that must be stated and tested outside Registry, or is it intentionally not an invariant despite normative rule 2?
options: State it as a release/installation invariant and require an external witness.
Declare it only a normative result and explain why State 2 does not treat the equality as a formal invariant.
open_points.default_guess: State it as a release/installation invariant; its witness belongs outside checks of Registry's code.

witness.initial: A release names dependencies A and B with their exact versions and digests, but the installed runtime also contains and loads dependency C.
events: The release process creates the release.
The installation installs A, B and the additional dependency C.
outcomes: Rule 2 is treated as a formal invariant, so the release or installation is rejected because the running dependency set differs.
The “Formal invariants: None” passage is followed, so no invariant witness is required and the additional dependency can escape the stated Required test.
witness.observer: The owner or security reviewer examining what code the production release can run.

open_points.subject: A20 Required tests item 1
open_points.text: Installing the release with a dependency whose digest differs fails.
open_points.question: What population must this Required tests item show the refusal for: one representative dependency, every declared dependency, or every dependency class named by rule 1, including the Python runtime and base image where the mismatch may be a version or image-digest mismatch?
options: One representative Python package with a wrong digest.
Each declared Python distribution with a wrong digest.
Each dependency class in rule 1: Python packages, Python version and base image, using the applicable version or digest mismatch.
open_points.default_guess: Show refusal for each dependency class named by rule 1 and at least one declared package; otherwise the test does not demonstrate the full installation guarantee.

witness.initial: The release names the correct Python-package digests but names Python 3.x and a base-image digest different from those being installed.
events: The installation test exercises only a Python package whose distribution digest is changed.
That package mismatch is refused, so the written Required test passes.
A release is then installed with the wrong Python version or base image.
outcomes: A narrow reading accepts the test as complete even though the non-package mismatch was never shown to fail.
A broad reading requires the Python-version and base-image cases to fail as well.
witness.observer: The release engineer deciding whether the dependency guarantee has passed its required test.

open_points.subject: A20 dependency-change verification
open_points.text: A dependency changes only by a new release, verified as any release.
open_points.question: What must verification of a release with changed dependencies establish: merely that the ordinary release checks ran, or specifically that the new dependency identities, exact versions, digests and absence of runtime external loading satisfy rules 1–4?
options: Ordinary release admission is sufficient, whatever it checks.
Verification must establish all dependency guarantees in rules 1–4 for the changed release.
Verification must establish only the changed dependency's version and digest.
open_points.default_guess: Require release verification to establish rules 1–4 for the complete resulting runtime dependency set.

witness.initial: A new release changes one package and introduces a dependency that loads a plugin from outside the release at runtime.
events: The release passes the ordinary application tests.
The changed dependency's distribution digest matches the release metadata.
The dependency later loads external plugin code.
outcomes: “Verified as any release” means ordinary release checks, so the release is admitted.
Verification includes A20 rules 1–4, so the release is refused for runtime external loading.
witness.observer: The owner and users relying on the claim that only verified code runs.

open_points.subject: A20 runtime code-loading boundary
open_points.text:
Registry has no dependency that loads code at run time from outside its
release.
open_points.question: Does the prohibition cover every path by which Registry can load runtime code from outside the release, including loading initiated directly by Registry's own code, or only such loading performed by a component classified as a dependency?
options: Only dependencies are forbidden from loading external runtime code.
Registry and every dependency are forbidden from loading any runtime code from outside the release.
Registry may load external code only through a separately declared and verified mechanism.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the prohibition to Registry and all of its dependencies, preserving the stated consequence that what runs is what was verified.

witness.initial: Registry's own module, rather than a third-party dependency, contains a configurable plugin loader.
events: The release and every named dependency pass digest verification.
Registry's own loader imports a plugin stored outside the release.
outcomes: The literal dependency-only reading permits the load because no dependency performed it.
The whole-runtime reading refuses or prevents the load because the plugin is outside the verified release.
witness.observer: The security reviewer and the owner of the running installation.
